# Third-party register

Every **direct** dependency of Bugaboo — shipped or used only for building, testing or docs — has one row here, added in the same change that adds the dependency (coding-standards §5). The register check (`cargo xtask check only DEP-REGISTER`, coding-standards §7) compares these tables with `Cargo.lock` and the npm lockfiles and fails on any difference.

Together with the lockfiles, this register is the source for the SBOM, the third-party notices and *About › Licenses* (COMP-01, COMP-02).

Columns:

- **Ships?** — *yes* if it ends up in the Bugaboo binary or browser app; *no* for build, test and docs tools.
- **Health** — maintained / slow / unmaintained, plus the date checked.
- **Alternatives** — what else was considered and why not.

## Bundled data

Data files that are built into the program. They are not packages, so the checks do not compare them with a lockfile; this table is the register.

| Data | Source | License | Ships? | Purpose | Notes |
|------|--------|---------|--------|---------|-------|
| `crates/bb-auth/data/breached-passwords.txt` | [SecLists](https://github.com/danielmiessler/SecLists) `Passwords/Common-Credentials/xato-net-10-million-passwords-1000000.txt` and `Pwdb_top-1000000.txt` (copied 2026-10-04) | MIT (SecLists, Copyright (c) 2018 Daniel Miessler) | yes | The check against breached passwords when a password is set (AUTH-01). No network call at runtime | The two lists hold passwords from public leaks. The file keeps only entries of 12 to 24 printable ASCII characters (shorter ones fail the length rule anyway), in lower case, without duplicates, sorted bytewise: see the file, under 1 MiB. A password is looked up in lower case. Refresh by repeating the filter on newer lists |

## Accepted risks

| Advisory | Package | Severity | Why accepted | Re-check |
|----------|---------|----------|--------------|----------|
| [GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) | braces (3.0.3, via stylelint, globby, fast-glob, micromatch) | high (stack exhaustion through deeply nested patterns) | No patched release exists: the advisory covers every version, and the only suggested fix downgrades stylelint to 7.7.0. The package is a dev-only tool (stylelint globbing our own files); it is not shipped and never receives untrusted patterns. | 2027-01-04, or when braces, micromatch or stylelint publish a new release |
| [RUSTSEC-2023-0071](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071) | rsa 0.9.10 (via webauthn-rs, for the RSA passkeys some devices make) | medium (the Marvin attack: timing leaks when a *private* RSA key decrypts or signs) | Bugaboo only *verifies* RSA signatures with public keys, which the attack does not touch; no private RSA key exists on the server. No patched release of `rsa` 0.9 exists | When `rsa` 0.10 is final and webauthn-rs uses it (M1-F36) |
